comment: N-019 (2026-09-12): the shared default 0.8/0.1/0.1 temporal split left the test half sitting on the dead tail of the recording -- source annotations collapse after ~84% of the timeline, so the 10% test block held only 228 forecast windows (18 after eval-stride dedup, over 12 tracks). The user instructed a 50/50 split with the first half divided 40/10, 'consistent with prior work' (verbatim, 2026-09-12 decisions batch): 'I believe Grand Central should be 50/50 split. and from the first 50, we can do 40/10. Consistent with prior work. We will want to use it to fine-tune.' A repository-wide search (issue-finder-deep, N-019 investigation, 2026-09-12) found no recorded citation for that prior-work convention anywhere in this repository or the vendored references/opentraj checkout; the ratios below implement the reading 40+10=50 ('the first 50') as train 0.4 / val 0.1 / test 0.5 over the whole timeline, i.e. the dense 0-50% of the recording is train+val and the test half (50-100%) absorbs the dead tail instead of only the last 10%. The citation for 'prior work' is still to be supplied by the user.
